name: Sitemaps
title: XML Sitemaps for GoCommerce — Open-Source Module
description: Publish a storefront sitemap from the live GoCommerce catalogue: products, collections and CMS pages, the storefront URL and paths, and the 50,000-URL limit.
ogDescription: Products, collections and pages from the live catalogue, with the day each last changed. Read from the source.
lede: A Go package that publishes the storefront’s sitemap from the live catalogue — every active product and collection, and every published page when the cms module is installed. It needs one setting: where the storefront lives.
what: The module serves a sitemap index at /x/sitemaps/sitemap.xml and the files it points at: products.xml, collections.xml and, with the cms module installed, pages.xml. Every URL carries the day the thing it names last changed.

The engine does not know where its storefront lives, so, as the package doc puts it, the address is a setting — and so are the paths, because storefronts differ on whether a product lives at /products/{slug} or /p/{slug}. A storefront serves /sitemap.xml by proxying or redirecting to the index.

The files are generated on request from the live catalogue and cacheable for an hour. Each carries a stylesheet instruction, so a person who opens one in a browser sees a table of what is listed rather than raw XML; crawlers ignore it.
configLede: One setting is required: the storefront’s URL. With it in Config the module starts switched on; otherwise switch it on and fill it in on the Plugins screen, which wins where both say something.

config.note: Where the pages live, e.g. https://shop.example. Until it is set the sitemap answers 409 and says so; while the plugin is off, 404.
The product page’s path with {slug} in it. Defaults to /products/{slug}; set it on the Plugins screen — see the limits.
The collection page’s path. Defaults to /collections/{slug}.
The content page’s path, used when the cms module is installed. Defaults to /pages/{slug}.

setup.t: Import it and pass sitemaps.New to gocommerce.New, as below — or run the reference binary with -sitemaps, which reads STOREFRONT_URL.
The storefront URL, and the product, collection and page paths if your storefront’s differ from the defaults, on the Plugins screen.
Have the storefront proxy or redirect /sitemap.xml to /x/sitemaps/sitemap.xml — and /x/sitemaps/ too, since the index links to the files there.
Open the index in a browser: the stylesheet shows what is listed. Then submit the storefront’s /sitemap.xml to the search engines.

codeNote: As the repository’s examples/store/main.go wires it, with its imports; cfg is your gocommerce.Config. The package doc itself has no example.

howItWorks.t: sitemap.xml lists products.xml and collections.xml, and pages.xml when the cms module is installed. All five routes are public and documented in the module’s OpenAPI file.
Each file is built on request from active products, active collections and published pages, read 500 at a time, and sent with Cache-Control: public, max-age=3600.
Every URL carries lastmod — the day it last changed, in UTC — and a change frequency: weekly for products and collections, monthly for content pages.
Each file points at a stylesheet the module serves beside it, so the first click after switching it on answers whether it worked.
The index’s links use the host the request came to, honouring X-Forwarded-Host and X-Forwarded-Proto, so behind a proxy they carry the storefront’s address.
Switched off, every file is a 404. Switched on without a storefront URL, a 409 that names the setting to fill in.

limits.t: The package doc names it: a sitemap file holds 50,000 URLs, and a catalogue past that needs the products file split, which this does not do yet.
The panel’s path fields have defaults, read before Config, so ProductPath, CollectionPath and PagePath in Config never take effect. Set the paths on the Plugins screen.
Products, collections and content pages only. Category pages are not listed.
Each entry is a location, a date and a frequency: no image entries, and no alternates for other languages.
The files are served by GoCommerce under /x/sitemaps/. The storefront has to proxy or redirect its /sitemap.xml; the module cannot answer at the storefront’s address.
It tells no search engine that something changed. That is the indexnow module’s job.

faq.q: Why is the sitemap served by the API and not the storefront?
faq.a: Because the catalogue lives there. The engine builds the files from live data; the storefront serves /sitemap.xml by proxying or redirecting to /x/sitemaps/sitemap.xml, as the package doc describes.

faq.q: My product pages are at /p/{slug}. What do I change?
faq.a: The product page path, on the Plugins screen. Set it there rather than in Config: the panel’s default of /products/{slug} is read first, so a path in Config is never used.
When the cms module is installed. The index then includes pages.xml, with every published page; without the cms module, pages.xml answers 404 and the index leaves it out.
As fresh as the catalogue: every file is built on request, and marked cacheable for an hour.
No. Any storefront that can proxy or redirect /sitemap.xml can use it; the paths are settings precisely because storefronts differ.
